title: Project Architecture
text:
This repository contains the source code for the RDA Domain Ambassadors website, built using Quarto. It is designed to be a modern, dynamic static site that centralizes resources and ambassador profiles for the Research Data Alliance community.



To keep the project organized as it grows and participants add more resources, we use a modular and scalable structure:



_quarto.yml: Main Quarto configuration (navigation, metadata, theme).
styles.scss: Custom styles (RDA colors, animations).
index.qmd, about.qmd: Main static pages.





docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Technical project documentation (this file).
docs/UPDATES.md: History of changes and updates.




Instead of creating a page for each resource, we use simple databases: - data/ambassadors.csv: Information about the ambassadors. - data/resources.csv: Metadata for all resources (title, author, domain, file link).



To avoid cluttering the root with .qmd files: - pages/ambassadors/index.qmd: Ambassadors directory. - pages/resources/index.qmd: Main resource search engine. - pages/contribute/index.qmd: Contribution guide for users.



This is where physical files (PDFs, images) are stored, organized logically to avoid chaos: - assets/images/ambassadors/: Profile pictures. - assets/resources/domains/agriculture/: Domain-specific documents for agriculture. - assets/resources/domains/humanities/: Humanities documents. - assets/resources/shared/: General guides (e.g., FAIR data principles) that apply to everyone.
This strict separation between code (.qmd), data (.csv), and files (assets/) ensures the repository remains easy to maintain even with thousands of resources.




To make contributions seamless, the site will implement a data-driven architecture. Instead of hardcoding resources into Markdown, structured data (e.g., lists of resources or ambassadors) will be pulled from data files (like data/resources.csv or data/ambassadors.csv). During the Quarto build process, this data is rendered dynamically. This empowers non-technical contributors to update the site simply by editing a spreadsheet or CSV file.



The site leverages Quarto’s built-in Bootstrap 5 integration: 1. Base Theme: Starting with the cosmo theme for a clean, professional baseline. 2. Customizations: The styles.scss overrides Bootstrap default variables to introduce a bespoke primary/secondary color palette. 3. Components: Custom utility classes (.hero-banner, .resource-card) are used extensively to create premium layouts and subtle animations that enhance user experience.

title: Updates & Changelog
text:
This document tracks all major updates, new features, and changes made to the RDA Domain Ambassadors website project.





Initialized core Quarto website project structure.
Created _quarto.yml for global site configuration, search, and navigation.
Added custom styling via styles.scss for a modern, responsive design and micro-animations.
Scaffolded core pages: index.qmd (homepage with hero banner), about.qmd, ambassadors.qmd, resources.qmd, and contribute.qmd.
Created ARCHITECTURE.md to document the technical stack, styling methodology, and content workflows.
Created UPDATES.md to serve as a persistent changelog.
Reorganized project structure into /data, /pages, /assets, and /docs for better scalability.
Translated all project documentation and site scaffolding to English.

title: Get Involved & Contribute
text: We welcome contributions from the entire RDA community! Whether you want to add a new guide, share a helpful video, or update an ambassador profile, you can do it here.

title: Get Involved & Contribute
text:
How to Contribute
Currently, the best way to add resources is by submitting a request or directly modifying our repository.

Option 1: Add a Resource

Navigate to our GitHub Repository (link coming soon).
Open the data/resources.csv file.
Add a new row with your resource details (Title, Type, Link).
Submit a Pull Request.



Option 2: Edit a Page
Found a typo or want to expand a section? You can edit any .qmd file in our repository. Quarto uses standard Markdown, making it easy to read and write.
Need help? Contact the site administrators.

title: About Us
text:
The RDA Domain Ambassadors are a network of disciplinary experts who bridge the gap between the global Research Data Alliance community and specific research domains.
These distinguished professionals work to navigate daily research data challenges while promoting RDA outputs and FAIR data principles within their respective fields.



Promote: Share FAIR data practices and RDA outputs.
Connect: Serve as a liaison between domain researchers and the RDA.
Support: Provide guidance, resources, and mentorship to domain communities.
